AddMemory.description:
Create a NEW memory (item + first revision). This is how anything gets stored: pick the
`kind` and give its `fields`. Say where it applies (`scope: universal`, or `anchors` /
`about`), or a directive is flagged as unscoped.

fields.description:
`text` (the whole statement, in one sentence) plus the kind's own fields, required first, optional in brackets:
fact (a standing statement about the world or the setup): text, subject (concept id, e.g. concept:python), predicate, object (text or a concept id)
directive (a rule for how you should behave; say where it applies: `scope: universal`, or anchors / about): text, strength (must|should|prefer), rule [polarity (do|avoid), rationale]
decision (a choice that was made, with what it was chosen over): text, chosen, rationale, decided_at (ISO datetime) [alternatives (list of str)]
event (something that happened at a particular time): text, occurred_at (ISO datetime) [participants (list of str), outcome]
procedure (ordered steps to follow: ONE memory for the whole procedure): text, trigger, steps (list of {text, optional}) [preconditions (list of str)]
task (something to do later (a reminder)): text [due (ISO datetime), state (open|done|cancelled)]
lesson (what a failure taught, to apply next time): text, situation, insight [do_instead]
Every kind also takes: scope (contextual|universal|topical|reference), anchors, about (concept ids), qualifiers, expires_at, confidence. Do not repeat `kind` inside `fields`.
fields.title: Fields

EditChange.description:
Say the same thing better: a clearer label, a tighter definition, other names. The meaning
must not change (otherwise define a new concept and deprecate this one); the id never does.
The previous label stays as an alias.

Evidence.description:
What a memory comes from: words that were said, or an external source it cites.

Words that were said: give a `quote` and the daemon looks it up among your recent episodes (it
must occur there literally, case and spacing aside); nothing is stored when it does not. Give an
`episode` id as well to name the exact message; the quote must then occur in that one.

A source: give `source` (a uri, and ideally a locator and a short literal quote). The daemon
stores the reference with the memory; it does not read the source or require that it exists.

episode.description: Optional: the episode id, when you know it.
episode.title: Episode

quote.description: Words from the conversation, copied literally (a sentence).
quote.title: Quote

source.description: An external source it comes from (instead of a quote).

Evidence.title: Evidence

Finding.description: One validation observation. `error` blocks the proposal; others are advice.
Finding.title: Finding

ForgetRequest.description:
Retire memories: one by id, or every active memory anchored under a path.

Nothing is deleted: each target gets a `retract` op, so the reason and the history stay.

IssuedCredential.description: The only time the token is ever shown.

LayerState.description: What the score layer is doing for one owner, and why.

LinkMemories.description:

nothing new: use `add` for that.

served unless it ranked the trusted requests worse (`reverted`).

OntologyCheck.description: A read-only report on the ontology's health (nothing is fixed automatically).

ResolveRequest.description:
Ask the daemon to do what the card proposes (as a proposal from you): `merge` keeps the
oldest memory of a duplicate cluster and supersedes the others; `supersede` lets the newer
memory of an update replace the older; `retract` retracts the memory of a feedback or expiry
task.
ResolveRequest.title: ResolveRequest

Resource.description:
A registered anchor. Containment is mostly syntactic (path segments); this record adds
explicit containment (`parents`) and equivalence (`same_as`) on top.
Resource.title: Resource

RestoreChange.description:
Put a concept back to the fields it had at an earlier version (also how an edit, a
deprecation or a merge is undone). It makes a new version; nothing is rewritten.
RestoreChange.title: RestoreChange

RetractMemory.description: Declare a memory wrong/polluted. Dependents derived from it are flagged stale.
RetractMemory.title: RetractMemory

ReviseMemory.description: New revision of an existing memory; `fields` overlay the current revision.
ReviseMemory.title: ReviseMemory

Signal.description: An observation about the environment, by concept id or label ("python", 3.12).
Signal.title: Signal

SourceCheckRequest.description:
Report what you found when you went back to a source: `ok` (as cited), `changed` (the
cited statement may no longer hold) or `missing`. `changed` and `missing` open a review task
for each memory that cites it.
SourceCheckRequest.title: SourceCheckRequest

SourceRef.description:
Where a statement comes from. Only `uri` is required; the rest makes a later check, or a
reader without access to the source, much more useful. Give a short `quote` copied literally
from the source: it stays with the memory even if the source is edited or deleted.

content_hash.description: Hash of the source as read (any scheme, e.g. sha256:…): lets a later check say whether it changed.
content_hash.title: Content Hash

locator.description: Where in it: page, section, lines, timestamp.
locator.title: Locator

quote.description: Words from the source, copied literally.
quote.title: Quote

uri.description: file:///path, https://…, doi:10.…, arxiv:…; canonicalised by the daemon.
uri.title: Uri

SourceRef.title: SourceRef

SplitChange.description:
One concept turned out to be several: the source is deprecated (kept as a tombstone) and
points to what it became. `into` are existing concepts (ids, labels) or new ones to define.
SplitChange.title: SplitChange

SupersedeMemory.description: `new` (a `ref` from this proposal, or an existing memory id) replaces `target`.
SupersedeMemory.title: SupersedeMemory

SupersessionReason.description: Why a revision was replaced (the `supersedes` edge's own fields).
SupersessionReason.title: SupersessionReason

TaskResult.description:
How a maintenance task was resolved. `merge` (a duplicate cluster), `supersede` (an
update), `retract` and `revise` (a memory reported wrong or expiring) must cite the proposal
that did it; `distinct` (two memories differ) and `keep` (the memory stands) are remembered and
not raised again; `defer` parks the task for later.
TaskResult.title: TaskResult

UnrelateChange.description: End one relation (the edge is kept as history).
UnrelateChange.title: UnrelateChange

UpdateCandidate.description:
The same statement with a changed value (a version, an amount, a date): `newer` probably
supersedes `older`. Not a duplicate: merging would lose the update.
UpdateCandidate.title: UpdateCandidate

info.description:
Structured, typed memory for agents. Writes go through **proposals** (validated, then
committed or held for review by policy); reads return current memories with their history.

Authentication: off by default (run on localhost only; the caller is then a label from
`X-Ontyra-Actor`, `X-Ontyra-Actor-Kind`, `X-Ontyra-Harness`). With `ONTYRA_AUTH__TOKEN` every
request needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. With `ONTYRA_AUTH__MULTI_USER` each account has
credentials (see `/v1/admin`); the account decides the owner, actor kind and permissions, and
the headers are ignored. An owner is never a request parameter.
